messages.subject: Colors in SNP plot
messages.body_plain:
Hi, everyone I hope you and your relatives are safe during this time.

I'm just curious (and maybe I'm asking a dumb question). In the SNP plots, the genes in the lower panel have a color... Is that color associated with the Strains/Variants/evaluated in these plots? or they mean something else? (I attached the image example of the QTL2 manual)

Thanks a have a nice week.

Juan C.

messages.subject: Re: Colors in SNP plot
messages.body_plain:
The genes colors are arbitrary. That part of the plot is made by plot_genes(). The argument colors: “Vectors of colors, used sequentially and then re-used.”

karl

messages.subject: Header-only chromosome files when processing Geneseek
messages.subject_clean: Header-only chromosome files when processing Geneseek
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl/all,

We're starting a new project looking for linkage between a fatal/nonfatal phenotype associated with an AJ mouse strain after a cross with NOD mice. We're eventually going to do Collaborative Cross mice, so we're using QTL2 to start to analyze GigaMUGA data.

We're using the Preparing DO mice tutorial to start. However when using the geneseek2qtl2.R script, it generates 21 chromosome files with headers only.

Any ideas?

Best and thanks!
Randall Marshall
Cincinnati Children's Hospital
Prows lab, Department of Human Genetics

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Header-only chromosome files when processing Geneseek
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl2-disc] Header-only chromosome files when processing Geneseek
messages.body_plain:
I think the header in the finalreport file is causing the problem. Try adding "skip=9" in the line
    g <- myfread(ifile)
to skip over that header. So it's like this:

    g <- myfread(ifile, skip=9)
karl
